reviews.comment: Lots of tough material and he will move fast through it, but he makes the exams (85% of your grade) very fair, with plenty of past exams to practice, and has exam reviews. Reading the textbook or supplementary material is necessary as he will likely not cover it all in class. Homework takes some time and is from the textbook. Very entertaining guy!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are 85% of your grade. He's nice and a little funny during lectures, but you really need to catch on to every word he says. He doesn't always talk about everything in class, so use the textbook too. Sometimes he lectures really quick and skips some steps. Make sure to ask questions in class. You'll need to study really hard for exams.

PHYS 309 is a survey class, so we covered a lot of topics really fast. Belyanin's lectures are extremely dense, but he peppers them with quips about his time in the Soviet Union, random out-of-pocket physics drama, and occasionally he will pause lecturing, look out at the class, and ask, "Scared?" Drink from the fire hose, and chew on the homework.

He's a very difficult professor to get. His lectures are difficult to follow, and even when you visit him outside of class hours it's pretty hard to understand what he means. HW also doesn't accurately reflect test material. Class is 85% tests so be mindful. He posts previous tests which was helpful. Be wary of him.

The lecture slides weren't useful but he went over what would be on the exam during reviews. Attendance is 5%. Overall the homework is how you learn the course content was very similar to what was featured on the exam. He holds a lot of office hours. Honors section had only slightly more challenging hw and exams, so I would recommend taking it.

I hate to say this because Dr. Belyanin is a funny and personable prof, he's just not the best at teaching an introductory course. He just seems too smart to be teaching this class, and the work was very intense. Final is 40% of your grade, and only one midterm that is 30%, avg for midterm was ~50. Definitely would be better for advanced physics.
My favorite quotes from him are, "Quantum mechanics is common sense" and "Remember this from kindergarten?"
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy
